nodes.label: Cold Fusion Under a Closed Index (paper)
nodes.rationale: Three moves, each a chapter of the method run on a question the book did not ask: a refusal derived three ways, a computation the refusal points at, and a reduction from 'achievable?' to laboratory equalities. Every number preceded the sentence describing it, and both predictions were committed before their computations ran.

nodes.label: The Refusal on Three Routes
nodes.rationale: By the law (E(Λ) = 0, so a complete index makes exactly zero predictions), by the coordinates (all eight are electronic and the bracket is measurably blind to Z — the Chapter 11 wrong-charge episode held 56 of 56 while the charge was wrong), and by the data (ⅅ_phys terminates outside the index with no reproducible levels to bracket). The refusal is the theorem applied, not caution.

nodes.label: The Nuclide Chart as an Index on (Z, N)
E(measured nuclide chart, Z ≤ 9) = 9
nodes.rationale: 77 cells in, 86 in ℛ(X), nine holes and X ⊆ ℛ(X) exactly — the chart is not denied by its own bounds, it is simply not closed. Eight of the nine holes have odd N, so E is the pairing interaction made visible as an indexing defect; the drawn monotone-band chart is precisely ℛ of the measured one, and the drawing hides the physics by filling the holes.

nodes.label: Holes as Exit Channels — Non-Closure as Mechanism
nodes.rationale: d + t proceeds and releases 17.59 MeV because (2,3) is a hole — there is no bound ⁵He to hold the product together — and helium burning stalls because (4,4) is one. Where the compound cell is a hole the reaction is fast and its products dictated; where it is occupied the energy must leave electromagnetically and the reaction is slow. The chart's failure to close is, cell for cell, the mechanism.

nodes.label: Three Commensurability Equalities per Watt
nodes.rationale: Per watt of claimed excess heat: 1.91×10¹² n-channel events/s, 1.55×10¹² t+p, 2.62×10¹¹ ⁴He+γ. Vacuum branching then demands 8.55×10¹¹ neutrons/s/W and the ⁴He branch 3.76×10⁻⁸ mol/W·day, so the historical claims require a ~10⁷ branching shift with the 23.85 MeV gamma suppressed — itself a nuclear claim needing its own two-route evidence.

nodes.label: The Value-Set Escape (ℛ on sparse coordinates)
nodes.rationale: ²⁸F and ³⁰F are exact analogues of the counted holes but vanish from ℛ(X)\X because no bound nuclide in the window has N = 19 or 21 at all: a hole in a value set is invisible to a reconstruction built on value sets. Recorded as a statement about the operator, making E = 9 a lower bound.

nodes.label: Register Entry R1 — the Nuclide-Chart Row Corrected
nodes.rationale: The book's row 'nuclide chart with drip lines, 383 cells, E = 0, self-defining' conflates the drawn band with the measurement; idempotence ℛ(ℛ(X)) = ℛ(X) was verified, so the row should name the band and the band–measurement difference should be recorded as content.

nodes.label: ℛ(X) and E(X) as External Definition Cost
nodes.rationale: On two coordinates ℛ specialises to a two-sided cumulative running-maxima staircase, and a set is ℛ-closed iff it is exactly such a staircase — which is why a drawn drip line closes automatically and a measured one does not.

nodes.label: ⁸Be, the Even–Even Exception and the Triple-Alpha Bottleneck
nodes.rationale: The one hole the odd-N parity pattern cannot explain is explained by alpha clustering: (4,4) is missing, so stellar helium burning routes around it through a resonance.

nodes.label: Appendix B Translated Bench-ward
nodes.rationale: Admissibility, a committed-prediction sheet, declines and the file drawer, nulls as bounds (the 1,061 move) and the grid, offered as a calorimetry protocol — the register of five entries for one short paper being the method applied to its own production.
